core_gameplay_loop: Designed for a 10-minute mobile session structured into four phases: 1) Morning Check (1.5 min): Harvest crops from paddy and swidden plots, collect coconut tuba sap, and inspect coastal fish traps; 2) Island Expedition & Trade (4 min): Set sail on an outrigger proa canoe to a neighboring island or reef, engaging in barter trade, hunting, or gathering; 3) Rebuilding & Crafting (2.5 min): Use collected rattan, timber, and fibers to craft items or contribute to communal village restoration (bayanihan); 4) Evening Rest & Trust Ritual (2 min): Gift surplus commodities to the communal pantry or village chieftain, boosting Village Trust before resting to refresh stamina for the next day cycle.
farming_mechanics: Employs a dual plot system reflecting authentic precolonial island agriculture: Wet Paddy (Sawah) for water-intensive crops like Palay, requiring monsoon rains or manual irrigation; and Dry Swidden (Kaingin) for drought-tolerant roots like Kamote and Gabi. Soil health is managed through crop rotation and fish offal composting. Weather drives hydration—the Habagat monsoon automates watering, whereas the Amihan dry season demands bamboo irrigation work. Growth timers match session pacing, allowing crops to mature across 1-3 play sessions.
trading_mechanics: A pure barter economy operating on relative value matrices rather than monetary currency. Merchants evaluate offers based on regional scarcity, utility, and seasonal demand—for example, coastal settlements overvalue timber and grains, while inland river communities overvalue salt, fish, and sea oils. The trading interface uses a visual balance scale that weighs offered goods against requested inventory. Players can perform haggling ('Tawad') or offer bonus ceremonial gifts to tip trade scales favorably.
day_night_cycle: A 10-minute real-time day cycle divided into Morning (2 min - farming & trap prep), Midday (4 min - island voyages, foraging, bartering), Evening (2 min - crafting, communal dining, trust gifting), and Night (2 min - shelter fortification, storm warnings, stamina sleep). The climate transitions every 7 in-game days across three seasons: Amihan (Northeast Monsoon - clear skies, steady sailing), Habagat (Southwest Monsoon - heavy rains, boosted crop growth, turbulent seas), and Unos (Storm Season - devastating weather surges, isolated trade routes, emergency shelter preservation).

village_trust_system: Village Trust is a collective socio-cultural metric ('Bayanihan System') that replaces individual monetary wealth. Players build Trust by depositing surplus food into the communal storehouse, rebuilding destroyed village dwellings, and gifting luxury items like Tuba or Agila during communal gatherings. Higher Trust tiers unlock community-assisted farming labor, access to shared village proa vessels, lower trade profit margins with allied islanders, and access to sacred crafting knowledge. Neglecting communal obligations or hoarding rare supplies during storm disasters triggers Trust decay, restricting progression until community reparations are made.
economy_balance_notes: Economy balance relies on organic decay sinks and dynamic seasonal demand spikes rather than gold sinks. Raw organic goods decay over time if unpreserved (e.g., fresh Bangus spoils into low-grade fertilizer within 2 days unless salted or smoked), encouraging constant resource rotation. Supply and demand fluctuate dramatically around the storm cycle: pre-Unos periods cause massive demand spikes for preserved foods (Kalamay, dried fish) and shelter timber, while post-Unos recovery periods double the trade value of building materials (Nipa fronds, Rattan). Sacred non-perishables like Mutya Pearls and Agila resin serve as stable high-value trade anchors.
